I need to determine the molecular formula of a molecule in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry using ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique. 

Mass spectrometry will give me mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios of ions, which can help me determine the molecular weight of the compound. From the molecular weight and the mass spectrum pattern, I can deduce the molecular formula.

Let me start by obtaining the mass spectrometry data.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak at m/z 180.04225873612 (100% intensity)
- M+1 peak at m/z 181.0456536808673 (9.98% intensity)
- M+2 peak at m/z 182.04740106429998 (1.27% intensity)

The base peak at m/z 180.042 likely represents the [M+H]+ or [M-H]- ion depending on the ionization mode. Given this is ESI, it could be either positive or negative mode.

If this is [M+H]+, the molecular weight would be approximately 179.042.
If this is [M-H]-, the molecular weight would be approximately 181.042.

Let me analyze the isotope pattern:
- The M+1 peak is about 10% of the base peak, which suggests the presence of carbon atoms (each carbon contributes ~1.1% to M+1 due to 13C)
- 10% / 1.1% ≈ 9 carbon atoms

The M+2 peak at 1.27% could indicate oxygen atoms or other elements.

For a molecular weight around 179-181 with approximately 9 carbons (108 mass units), I need to account for the remaining ~71-73 mass units.

Common molecular formulas around this mass:
- C9H8O4 = 180.042 (9×12 + 8×1 + 4×16 = 108 + 8 + 64 = 180)

Let me verify: C9H8O4 has exact mass = 180.0423
This matches perfectly with the observed m/z 180.04225873612!

The isotope pattern also fits:
- 9 carbons would give ~9.9% M+1 (matches the 9.98% observed)
- 4 oxygens would contribute to M+2 peak

This is likely aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) or a similar compound with formula C9H8O4.
</thought>
